citation.title: Scaling atom-by-atom inverse design using nano-topology optimization and diffusion models
citation.version_coded: arXiv v1 (full text with supplementary notes; March 24, 2026)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: At a target mass ratio of 59.60%, the generic Gaussian diffusion model's best candidate reaches normalized stiffness 0.736, below the best Nano-TO design's 0.820.
claim.key_phrase: remains below the best Nano-TO design
claim.location: Results, Design of nanocantilevers under thickness-periodic boundary conditions using c-DDPM
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No speed-up is stated or derivable from reported runtimes.
claim.alternatives: The separate TO-DDPM production run reaches 0.860 against Nano-TO's 0.820; Supplementary Note A.10 also reports a selected TO-DDPM design at 0.822, 0.28% above the Nano-TO best (Results; Supplementary Note A.10).

baseline.classical_method: Atom-by-atom Nano-TO using non-learned stiffness optimization; the primary comparator is its best design at the same 59.60% mass ratio (Results, c-DDPM section).
baseline.implementation: LAMMPS atomistic simulation with the Mishin embedded-atom method potential and conjugate-gradient relaxation (Methods).
baseline.solver: Conjugate-gradient energy minimization for atomistic relaxation (Methods).
baseline.hardware_ml: NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU for c-DDPM training (Methods).
baseline.problem_size: 150,480 atoms (148,500 active) for thickness-periodic nanocantilevers; c-DDPM represents the cross-section as an image (Results; Methods).
baseline.classical_iterations: Nano-TO uses 64 independent trials per target mass ratio; max 100,000 minimization iterations per energy minimization (Results; Methods).
baseline.data_generation_cost: TO-DDPM training samples are reused from a pool of 48,000 Nano-TO designs; runtime to generate this pool is not stated (Results).
baseline.quality_metric: Normalized bending stiffness from atomistic energy-curvature calculations, at a fixed mass ratio (Results; Methods).
baseline.quality_gap: Gaussian-DDPM best 0.736 versus Nano-TO best 0.820 at mass ratio 59.60% (Results).

R1.evidence: The primary outcome compares design stiffness at equal target mass ratio; it makes no speed claim (Results, c-DDPM section).

R2.evidence: Methods identify LAMMPS with conjugate-gradient atomistic relaxation, but no timing comparison establishes an inefficient classical baseline.

R3.evidence: The diffusion-model result is a quality comparison, with no speed claim to assess for cost accounting (Results, c-DDPM section).

R4.evidence: Results state that generated designs are converted to atomistic models and evaluated for bending stiffness at the target mass ratio; a failure or infeasibility rate for generated outputs is not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Nano-TO: 64 trials per target mass ratio; Gaussian-DDPM training set: 32,000 layouts; TO-DDPM training pool: 48,000 designs, 32,000 retained; production generation: 32,000 samples (Results).

notes: The paper reports disconnected layouts removed from Nano-TO training data and transient floating atoms during Nano-TO optimization, but gives no invalid-output rate for generated diffusion candidates. Code is stated to be public; no reuse license or benchmark runtime is stated in the article.
